papers.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
papers.summary: Abstract Proteins are essential to life, and understanding their structure can facilitate a mechanistic understanding of their function. Through an enormous experimental effort 1–4 , the structures of around 100,000 unique proteins have been determined 5 , but this represents a small fraction of the billions of known protein sequences 6,7 . Structural coverage is bottlenecked by the months to years of painstaking effort required to determine a single protein structure. Accurate computational approaches are needed to address this gap and to enable large-scale structural bioinformatics. Predicting the three-dimensional structure that a protein will adopt based solely on its amino acid sequence—the structure prediction component of the ‘protein folding problem’ 8 —has been an important open research problem for more than 50 years 9 . Despite recent progress 10–14 , existing methods fall far short of atomic accuracy, especially when no homologous structure is available. Here we provide the first computational method that can regularly predict protein structures with atomic accuracy even in cases in which no similar structure is known. We validated an entirely redesigned version of our neural network-based model, AlphaFold, in the challenging 14th Critical Assessment of protein Structure Prediction (CASP14) 15 , demonstrating accuracy competitive with experimental structures in a majority of cases and greatly outperforming other methods. Underpinning the latest version of AlphaFold is a novel machine learning approach that incorporates physical and biological knowledge about protein structure, leveraging multi-sequence alignments, into the design of the deep learning algorithm.

papers.newspaper_title: AlphaFold的突破有条件：结构预测越过同源性门槛，但证据仍锁定在CASP14
papers.dek: 论文将物理与生物知识、多序列比对嵌入神经网络，在CASP14中展示了多数案例达到与实验结构相当的准确度；但现有证据支持的是结构预测能力，而不是对蛋白功能或所有分布的普适保证。
papers.background_and_pain: 蛋白三维结构预测长期受限于实验结构解析的高成本：确定单个结构可能需要数月至数年，而已解析结构只覆盖已知蛋白序列中的很小部分。既有计算方法尤其难以在缺少同源结构时达到原子级准确度，因此论文将问题聚焦于仅凭氨基酸序列预测蛋白结构，并尝试处理这一最具挑战性的情形。
core_innovations: 完全重新设计神经网络模型，将物理和生物学知识、多序列比对信息纳入深度学习算法的设计。
论文声称该方法在缺少相似已知结构时也能经常达到原子级结构预测准确度，从而针对同源性不足这一关键瓶颈提出解决方案。
papers.experimental_findings: 在CASP14这一具有挑战性的蛋白结构预测评测中，论文报告AlphaFold在多数案例上达到与实验结构相当的准确度，并显著优于其他方法。反例和适用边界同样重要：摘要使用的是“多数案例”和“经常达到”，并未支持所有蛋白、所有结构状态或所有后续功能任务上的普遍成功；候选信息也没有给出按蛋白类别、分布外条件或失败案例划分的详细结果。因此，不能把CASP14上的结构预测优势直接外推为蛋白功能理解或一般机制发现能力。

papers.title: Hippocampal sharp wave‐ripple: A cognitive biomarker for episodic memory and planning
papers.summary: Sharp wave ripples (SPW-Rs) represent the most synchronous population pattern in the mammalian brain. Their excitatory output affects a wide area of the cortex and several subcortical nuclei. SPW-Rs occur during "off-line" states of the brain, associated with consummatory behaviors and non-REM sleep, and are influenced by numerous neurotransmitters and neuromodulators. They arise from the excitatory recurrent system of the CA3 region and the SPW-induced excitation brings about a fast network oscillation (ripple) in CA1. The spike content of SPW-Rs is temporally and spatially coordinated by a consortium of interneurons to replay fragments of waking neuronal sequences in a compressed format. SPW-Rs assist in transferring this compressed hippocampal representation to distributed circuits to support memory consolidation; selective disruption of SPW-Rs interferes with memory. Recently acquired and pre-existing information are combined during SPW-R replay to influence decisions, plan actions and, potentially, allow for creative thoughts. In addition to the widely studied contribution to memory, SPW-Rs may also affect endocrine function via activation of hypothalamic circuits. Alteration of the physiological mechanisms supporting SPW-Rs leads to their pathological conversion, "p-ripples," which are a marker of epileptogenic tissue and can be observed in rodent models of schizophrenia and Alzheimer's Disease. Mechanisms for SPW-R genesis and function are discussed in this review.

papers.newspaper_title: 机制描述不等于算法解释：海马回放研究的迁移边界
papers.dek: 这篇跨主题候选以哺乳动物海马sharp wave–ripple为对象，提供了较完整的生物机制链条；但它不研究机器学习训练或损失地形，适合作为机制研究的对照，而非今日主题的直接证据。
brief_points: 摘要将SPW-Rs与CA3兴奋性递归系统、CA1快速网络振荡、抑制性中间神经元的时空协调以及压缩式序列回放联系起来，并讨论其对记忆巩固、决策和规划的作用。
摘要还描述了选择性破坏SPW-Rs会干扰记忆，以及生理机制改变可能形成与癫痫发生组织相关的病理性“p-ripples”；这些是所述生物系统内部的失效或病理状态。
不能将回放、记忆巩固或规划的生物学关联直接迁移为表示学习、上下文学习或优化动力学结论；候选信息未提供机器学习模型或训练实验。
